AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  VIA TELECONFERENCE ONLY
 Welcome to Glendale City Hall. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and
 rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the
 proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings are also archived on the
 City Website for viewing anytime at https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal.
 If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact
 the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required
 for requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
 related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
 meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
 Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  JUNE 17, 2021 AT 2:00 PM

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission meeting will be
available to the public electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

For public comments and questions during the meeting call (818) 937-8100.
 City staff will be submitting these questions and comments in real time to the appropriate person
during the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission meeting.

  1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA – 2:00 PM
  Roll Call
  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the June 17, 2021
  Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission was Posted on June
  10, 2021 on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.
  2. CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the May 20, 2021 Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission

  3. INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal

  Arts & Culture Administrator

  4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes.
  Members of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.
  5. ACTION ITEMS
  a. Report on the Cultural Equity and Inclusion Plan

  Motion recommending that the Director of Library, Arts & Culture enter into a Professional
  Services Agreement— in an amount not to exceed $20,000 from the 2021-2022 Work
  Plan — with The Aspire Group, a cultural equity and inclusion consultant, to: (1) research
  and analyze the external and internal cultural programming of Glendale Library, Arts &
  Culture (GLAC) and the Arts and Culture Commission (ACC) through a lens of cultural
  equity and inclusion, (2) establish a cultural equity and inclusion plan which guides all
  culturally specific work of GLAC and ACC (including but not limited to: Calls for Artist,
  RFPs, RFQs, I.D.E.A. programming, etc.), and (3) train GLAC staff and ACC in best
  practices for facilitating conversations focused on cultural equity and inclusion, specifically
  in regards to working externally with community stakeholders and patrons of GLAC.

  6. DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2021 6-Month Work Plan Progress Updates
  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS
  i. Art Happens Anywhere – Projects Update
  ii. LeBasse Projects – RFQ Update
   iii. Mural Ordinance – Update
  iv. Beyond the Box – Application opens in June 2021
  2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS – No Update
  3. PERFORMING ARTS – No Update
  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update

  b. Marketing and Communications for Arts and Culture projects in Glendale

7. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS
9. ADJOURNMENT
  The next Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission is Thursday, July 15,
  2021, at 2:00 PM via teleconference only.

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, June 17, 2021 at 2:00 p.m.
1.  ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on June 17, 2021 at 2:10 p.m.
  •  Present: Commissioner Viar, Vidor, Zadorian, Chairperson Tufenkian
  •  Absent: Vice Chair Yank
  •  The Agenda for the June 17, 2021 Regular Meeting was posted on June 10, 2021 on the Bulletin Board
  outside City Hall.

2.  CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES) Approved AS Amended

  a.  Minutes of the May 20, 2021 Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission (Approved
  as Amended)
  • Commissioner Viar stated that she had a correction and stated that on item 5A recused herself
  of voting on Action and it should reflect as abstained.
  • In reference to the April 15, 2021 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting Minutes,
  Commissioner Vidor had a minor amendment under item Commission/Staff Comments section,
  she stated:
  o “I did not ask for the elaboration for a mural definition to be an ‘addenda’ - this word is
  being used improperly. What I requested was that the definition of mural should be
  expanded to include all surfaces in the built environment that could potentially hold a
  mural such as streets, roofs, walls sidewalks, public utilities, etc.”

  Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded: Commissioner Viar

  Ayes:  Commissioners Viar, Vidor, Chairperson Tufenkian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Vice-Chair Yank
  Abstain:  Commissioner Zadorian

3.  INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Arts and Culture Commission
  Administrator.
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts
  & Culture locations.

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Speaker(s): None

5.  ACTION ITEMS
  a. Report on the Cultural Equity and Inclusion Plan
  Motion recommending that the Director of Library, Arts & Culture enter into a Professional

  1
   Services Agreement— in an amount not to exceed $20,000 from the 2021-2022 Work Plan — with The
  Aspire Group, a cultural equity and inclusion consultant, to: (1) research and analyze the external and
  internal cultural programming of Glendale Library, Arts & Culture (GLAC) and the Arts and Culture
  Commission (ACC) through a lens of cultural equity and inclusion, (2) establish a cultural equity and
  inclusion plan which guides all culturally specific work of GLAC and ACC (including but not limited to:
  Calls for Artist, RFPs, RFQs, I.D.E.A. programming, etc.), and (3) train GLAC staff and ACC in best
  practices for facilitating conversations focused on cultural equity and inclusion, specifically in regards to
  working externally with community stakeholders and patrons of GLAC.

 •  Ms. Fukutomi Jones gave a brief update and Commission asked questions and gave their input.

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby recommends that the Director of Library, Arts & Culture
  enter into a Professional Services Agreement— in an amount not to exceed $20,000 from the 2021-
  2022 Work Plan— with The Aspire Group, a cultural equity and inclusion consultant, to: (1) research
  and analyze the external and internal cultural programming of Glendale Library, Arts & Culture (GLAC)
  and the Arts and Culture Commission (ACC) through a lens of cultural equity and inclusion, (2)
  establish a cultural equity and inclusion plan which guides all culturally specific work of GLAC and ACC
  (including but not limited to: Calls for Artist, RFPs, RFQs, I.D.E.A. programming, etc.), and (3) train
  GLAC staff and ACC in best practices for facilitating conversations focused on cultural equity and
  inclusion, specifically in regards to working externally with community stakeholders and patrons of
  GLAC., as more fully outlined in the June 17, 2021 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Arts &
  Culture Administrator.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded:  Commissioner Viar

  Ayes: Commissioners Viar, Vidor, Zadorian, Chairperson Tufenkian
  Noes: None
  Absent: Vice-Chair Yank
  Abstain: None

6. DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2021 6-Month Work Plan Progress Updates
  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS
  i. Art Happens Anywhere – Projects Update
  • Ms. Fukutomi Jones stated that staff is currently working with the remaining 9 artists to facilitate the
  launch of their projects and also working with artist, Ayumi Chilsolm, to set an installation date for his
  mural at the YMCA entitled, “Yoshito Meditating in the Woods,” in August 2021
  • Commission asked questions and gave their input.

  ii. LeBasse Projects – RFQ Update
 •  Staff has been working with LeBasse Projects to develop a process for releasing RFQs for public art
  based on locations discussed at the May 20, 2021 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting.
  LeBasse Projects is currently in the process of preparing the RFQs which will be available on the
  Submittable platform to receive applications, and Staff will include the RFQ application link to the Arts
  and Culture Commission’s website (www.glendaleartsandculture.org). LeBasse Projects is working on
  drafting RFQ verbiage for 8 specific installations, and will place 2 specific installations on hold until final
  locations are decided. The RFQs are anticipated to be released in mid-July 2021. Staff will provide an
  update on the RFQs at the July17, 2021 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting.
 •  Commission asked questions and gave their input.

  iii. Mural Ordinance – Update
 •  Staff met with Sarah Odenkirk to discuss the current status of mural approval processes and procedures
  in Glendale. Ms. Odenkirk is currently in the process of reviewing Glendale Municipal Code 30.47 in
  2
   addition to the current mural approval processes and procedures. Ms. Odenkirk will be drafting
  recommendations on policies and procedures for artists’ submitting and the City’s processing murals on
  private property and City property, in addition to criteria for the Commission’s evaluating and approving
  the murals. Staff will provide an update on the mural approval processes and procedures in Glendale at
  the July 17, 2021 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting.

  iv. Beyond the Box – Application opens in June 2021
 •  Staff will be releasing the Beyond the Box Application on June 28, 2021. This year’s theme is
  “Celebrating our People with Disabilities Community,” and artists will be encouraged to submit a design
  proposal prior to the application deadline of August 6, 2021.
 •  Commission asked questions and gave their input.

  2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS – No Update

  3. PERFORMING ARTS – No Update

  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update

  b. Marketing and Communications for Arts and Culture projects in Glendale
 •  Staff discussed marketing and communications for the arts and culture projects in Glendale. Commission
  asked questions and gave their input.

7. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  • Commission thanked Ms. Fukutomi Jones and Staff for their hard work.

8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS: None

9. ADJOURNMENT 2:45 pm

The next Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission is Thursday, July 15,
2021, at 2:00 PM in City Council Chambers (2nd Floor) 613 E. Broadway,
